purpose: SNAPSHOT BEFORE EXECUTION AND BEFORE REVIEW. Commits BATCH-a33cda's design exactly as the executor and both validators will read it: the opening decision DEC-20260915-428a17 and its ranking; H-ICPERF-2c57cc, which discharges the two wordings H-ICPERF-cc4847 recorded as owed (Q1 now records the twist side, Q6 drops the mechanism attribution); the approved instrument-repair contract EXP-ICPERF-e21835 with its pre-registered acceptance table A1-A7; the drafted consuming row EXP-ICPERF-13f001 at approved_by null; and the review plan for REVIEW-ICPERF-20260915-a33cda together with its isolated R6 assignment. The executor task TASK-20260915-4f4027 depends on this archive precisely so that it starts from a committed, pushed contract rather than a working tree.
parent_sha_note: recorded in the archive block of dispatch_queue.json alongside commit_sha
commit_sha_note: A receipt cannot contain the hash of the commit that contains the receipt; the binding lives in this task's archive block in dispatch_queue.json and is verified by tools/research_dispatch.py.
binding_mode_note: content_at_commit FROM THE OUTSET, and this is the first batch designed that way (CORR-20260915-654160). This package deliberately contains records with a life after the archive: EXP-ICPERF-e21835 advances to `running` then `completed` then `analyzed`, EXP-ICPERF-13f001 from `draft` to `approved`, H-ICPERF-2c57cc onward from `specified`, and the goal head is reranked at every checkpoint. Under content_first -- which reads HEAD -- every one of those legitimate moves would report this archive as corrupt, which is exactly the failure CORR-20260915-654160 records against TASK-20260913-f8bdec. Reading the bytes in this archive's own commit asks the question a snapshot actually makes: did these records say this, when the executor read them.

not_hash_bound.coordination/goals/GOAL-ICPERF-e6b6a4/ba: Committed here and readable, but NOT hash-bound, because this archive's own commit_sha, parent_sha and path_sha256 are recorded into that file after this commit exists -- binding it would have no fixed point. Same treatment as every archive in BATCH-51e2aa. The cost, stated plainly: a later in-place edit to the queue is not caught by this receipt. It is caught elsewhere -- research_dispatch.py re-verifies every completed archive on every render, and tasks_state_revisions records queue repairs by hand.

self_hash_note: This receipt does not hash itself -- a file containing its own digest has no fixed point reachable by iteration. The queue entry archive.path_sha256 carries this file's hash, and research_dispatch.py verifies it there.
goal_head_binding_note: ledger/goals/GOAL-ICPERF-e6b6a4/goal.yaml is hash-bound here AND is declared by TASK-20260913-e74a82 in BATCH-51e2aa's queue. That is not double ownership -- ownership is checked within a queue -- and under content_at_commit the two bindings cannot contradict each other however often the head is reranked, because each reads the head's bytes in its own commit. Before CORR-20260915-654160 this was impossible, and BATCH-51e2aa was forced to disown the file and move it to also_staged_sha256 to keep its archive verifying.

base_commit_checked.merge_outcome: origin/main merged into this branch as d211fc8df before this archive was created; no conflict, so no superseding record was required. Never rebased: this branch carries pushed run records, and rebasing would rewrite the commits those receipts were archived in.
base_commit_checked.digest_acted_on: The merge digest for the range showed DEC-20260915-d8d413, which is this goal's OTHER lane deciding `revise` with approval WITHHELD on EXP-ICPERF-025a52. DEC-20260915-428a17 and the queue's disjointness note were rewritten to cite it as that lane's current state rather than the superseded DEC-20260915-674299. Nothing in the range touches this batch's records or this goal's head.

asserts_nothing_scientific: A snapshot is a custody act. It asserts that these bytes were committed before anything read them, and nothing whatever about whether the repair will pass its own acceptance, whether the Groebner column is measurable at l = 6, or whether any hypothesis here is true.
